sheet-1-1.description: Sheet 1, main part, shows the northern edge of the City of Plainfield along the Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left. It covers the ground between St. Mary's Avenue on the left and South Avenue on the right, from Hill Street at the top to Berckman Street at the bottom, with North Avenue running down the middle and the multiple tracks of the railroad between North Avenue and South Avenue. Much of the sheet is open land in large blocks (132 and 134), crossed by a small brook. St. Mary's Cemetery lies beyond St. Mary's Avenue at the left edge. Industry lines the railroad: the Plainfield Ice and Supply Company, with tank room, engine house, condensers and a track on a concrete trestle running to its storage building, stands between North Avenue and the tracks; on the far side of the tracks are coal pockets, the R. G. Bush cement block works and a bronze foundry near Berckman Street. Along South Avenue a row of frame dwellings faces the railroad, and a few dwellings stand on Hill Street and near Berckman Street at the bottom. The top right corner is taken by an inset showing the north end of block 134 on North Avenue (see part 2); the rest of the ground to the north is on sheet 53.
notes: St. Mary's Avenue is 'St Mary S Avenue' in OpenStreetMap.
The drawn railroad lies about 11 m from the modern Raritan Valley Line against the street points; the rail crossing was not used.

Map, 50 ft. St Mary's Av, North Av, South Av, Hill, Berckman, CRR of NJ; Plainfield Ice & Supply Co. Two parts: 1 main map; 2 boxed inset at top right showing the north end of block 134 on North Av (Recher & Co. and Standard Hair Co.), placed by two points carried from part 1.

sheet-1-2.description: Sheet 1, part 2, is a boxed inset in the top right corner of the sheet showing the northern end of block 134, between North Avenue and the Central Railroad of New Jersey, which lies just beyond the top edge of the main map. It is drawn at the same scale (50 feet to an inch) and orientation as the main part. Nearly the whole inset is taken by the works of Recher & Co. and the Standard Hair Co., combers and dyers of wool, mohair and hair: a long combing, draping and finishing building with saw-tooth skylights along North Avenue, an engine and dynamo house, a dye house, a reeling room, a pump room, a bleach house, a coal bin and a shed. A note gives the watchman, heating, lighting and fire protection of the works. The 16 inch water pipe in North Avenue is marked. The adjoining ground on three sides is on sheet 53, and the lower part of the block continues on the main part of sheet 1.
notes: No street junction in the inset: placed by two points carried from the main part (the same buildings are drawn at the top of the main map, about 985 px lower in the inset), with the main part's scale and rotation; low confidence.

Map, 50 ft. St Mary's Av, North Av, South Av, Hill, Berckman, CRR of NJ; Plainfield Ice & Supply Co. Two parts: 1 main map; 2 boxed inset at top right showing the north end of block 134 on North Av (Recher & Co. and Standard Hair Co.), placed by two points carried from part 1.

sheet-2-1.description: Sheet 2, main part, shows a residential corner of the City of Plainfield south of the railroad, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north at the top. Richmond Street crosses from the upper left and curves south to Putnam Avenue at the bottom; South Avenue and Scott Avenue bound the sheet at the top, East 6th Street and East 7th Street run across it from lower left to upper right, and Carlton Avenue runs down the right edge. A brook winds across the blocks between East 6th and East 7th Streets and another runs south from East 7th Street. Most buildings are frame dwellings, with a row of brick-veneered houses on East 6th Street and a wagon house near Scott Avenue. Block 238 between Richmond Street and Carlton Avenue is lined with dwellings on Carlton Avenue and Putnam Avenue. The lower left corner is taken by a boxed inset of the Plainfield Water Co. pumping station (part 2), placed over ground that continues on sheet 8, where East 6th Street runs on.
notes: The East 6th Street / Richmond Street junction was detected 7.6 m off the fit and rejected.
The inset of the Plainfield Water Co. pumping station (part 2) is not placed: it has no street and its location is not given on the sheet.

Map, 50 ft. South Av, Scott Av, E 6th St, E 7th St, Richmond St, Carlton Av, Putnam Av. Two parts: 1 main map; 2 boxed inset at lower left of the Plainfield Water Co. pumping station (not in place: East 6th St continues under it on sheet 8), not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Plainfield Water Co. pumping station (no street drawn and its location is not given on the sheet; needs the pumping station's location (a building or parcel corner) as anchor).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the eastern end of the Central Railroad of New Jersey yard in Plainfield, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Richmond runs down the left edge and is crossed by East 3rd, East 4th and East 5th Streets. East 3rd Street and North Avenue run across the upper part of the sheet toward Fillmore Avenue, and South Avenue runs along the bottom. Between North Avenue and South Avenue lies the wide railroad right of way lettered "C. R. R. of N. J.", with its bundles of through and yard tracks, a freight house with a platform beside it, a lumber platform and several spur tracks. The upper block, between East 3rd Street and North Avenue, holds a short row of frame dwellings on East 3rd Street (numbers 508 to 524), a large pink brick works with the Ideal Steam Laundry, an auto trimming and cement shop and a plumbing shop, a blue-tinted storage warehouse at the foot of Fillmore Avenue, and a group of frame dwellings and sheds along Fillmore Avenue. At the bottom stands the plant of Walter Scott & Co., Printing Press Mfrs., a long brick machine shop with numbered pattern, foundry and storage buildings, sprinklered and heated by its own works, with a note on its watchman's clock, fire pails and water supply. Cedar Brook appears in blue at the lower right corner. Water pipes (6 and 16 inch) and fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets. The sheet adjoins sheets 7 and 8 on the left, sheet 4 on the right and sheets 52, 2 and 55 beyond its edges.
notes: Printed streets match modern OpenStreetMap names: Richmond is Richmond Street.
The drawn Raritan Valley (Central Railroad of New Jersey) tracks lie about 29 m from the modern line; rail crossings were not used as control.
East 4th Street / Richmond Street junction was not detected (rail yard); the sheet is placed from six street junctions.
Map, 50 ft. Rail yard: Richmond, E 3rd, North Av, South Av, Fillmore, Scott; north upper right. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 continues the Central Railroad of New Jersey corridor in east Plainfield eastward from sheet 3, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. East 3rd Street crosses the top of the sheet, North Avenue and South Avenue run across the middle and bottom, Fillmore Avenue bounds the left side and Berckman bounds the right, with St. Mary's Avenue and Midway Avenue entering at the upper right. The upper block holds a row of frame dwellings fronting East 3rd Street (numbers 600 to 634), The Ebenezer Baptist Church at the corner of Fillmore Avenue, dwellings along Fillmore Avenue and Berckman, a large vacant factory building at the corner of North Avenue and Berckman, and an open interior with a few outbuildings. Between North Avenue and South Avenue the railroad right of way is drawn with parallel main tracks and a fan of yard sidings. North of the tracks stand the J. D. Loizeaux Lumber Co. East End Yard, with lumber sheds, an office and shingles storage, and the Plainfield Cement Stone Co. At the bottom, south of the tracks, are the Rushmore Dynamo Works, a group of foundry, machine shop, stock room and power buildings with concrete retaining walls along the railroad, and the east end of the Walter Scott plant from sheet 3. Cedar Brook crosses the bottom edge in blue. Water pipes, hydrants and a fire alarm box are marked in the streets. Adjoining sheet numbers 52, 55, 3, 0 and 1 are printed at the margins.
notes: Berckman is Berckman Street today; St. Mary's Avenue is St Mary S Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The drawn Raritan Valley (Central Railroad of New Jersey) tracks lie about 26 m from the modern line; rail crossings were not used as control.
Map, 50 ft. Fillmore, E 3rd, North, South, Berckman, St Mary's, Midway Av; rail yard. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 lies on the line between the City of Plainfield, Union County, and the Borough of North Plainfield, Somerset County, along Green Brook, and carries the printed title "Plainfield & North Plainfield". It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Green Brook winds from the top edge to the bottom edge, with the lettering "Borough of North Plainfield" on its west bank and "City of Plainfield" on its east bank. West of the brook, in North Plainfield, Manning Avenue runs down the left side and Brook Avenue follows the bank; Franklin Avenue crosses between them, Norwood Avenue forms the top boundary and Westervelt Avenue the lower one. The blocks hold detached frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys, a few with brick veneer, on rather loosely platted lots. East of the brook, in Plainfield, Sandford Avenue and Westervelt Avenue run east from the stream with dense rows of frame houses on narrow lots on both sides, Orange Place runs down the right edge and Elm Place crosses the bottom. A footbridge or street crossing links the two banks at Westervelt Avenue, and a pipe line and fire alarm box are marked. Block numbers 145 to 148, 114, 115, 112 and 113 are printed, with sheet numbers 9, 10, 6, 12 and 0 and 52 at the margins. The upper right is mostly blank and carries the north arrow.
notes: Franklin Avenue west of the brook corresponds to the modern west section of Sandford Avenue (inferred from block spacing; medium confidence).
Elm Place is part of modern Roosevelt Avenue; Elm Place and Roosevelt Avenue are separate names in OpenStreetMap.

Brook Avenue / Sandford Avenue was left out of the fit: the modern junction lies about 9 m east of the drawn one. The sheet is placed from four junctions, one on the sheet edge, so confidence is medium.

Map, 50 ft. Green Brook on the Plainfield / North Plainfield line; Norwood, Franklin (today west Sandford Av), Manning, Brook Av, Sandford, Westervelt. One part; Brook / Sandford left out (9 m off). Borders north-plainfield-1910 sheets 9, 10.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows a residential area of east Plainfield between Norwood Avenue at the top and Elm Place and Washington at the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. East Front runs down the middle of the sheet. To its left lie the blocks along Sandford Avenue and Westervelt Avenue as far as Orange Place, and a short North Front street between Westervelt Avenue and Elm Place; to its right a long block of lots runs from Richmond at the top to Washington at the bottom, with East 2nd Street along the right edge. Almost every lot carries a detached frame dwelling of two to two and a half storeys, many with rear stables or auto houses; a few are brick or brick veneer, among them a larger brick house with greenhouse buildings in the open ground at the upper left, and, on the East 2nd Street side, a cabinet making shop and an upholstering shop. A large part of the upper left, north of Sandford Avenue, is open ground belonging to one estate. Water pipes (4, 6, 8 and 16 inch) and hydrants are marked in the streets. Block numbers 113, 114, 115 and 116 are printed. The adjoining sheets are numbered 5 on the left, 7 on the right, 12 and 13 below and 52 above.
notes: Washington (east of East Front) and Elm Place (west) are the street now called Roosevelt Avenue.
East Front is East Front Street today; Richmond is Richmond Street.
Modern East 2nd Street lies about 8 m from the drawn street and was left out of the fit as displaced.
Map, 50 ft. E Front, Sandford, Westervelt, Orange Pl, Elm Pl, Washington (today Roosevelt Av). One part; East 2nd St left out (modern line 6-8 m off).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows a long, narrow strip of east Plainfield between Richmond at the top and Washington at the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Three parallel streets run down the page, East 2nd Street on the left, East 3rd Street in the middle and Cottage Place on the right, with the broad Central Railroad of New Jersey right of way and East 4th Street beyond it. The blocks are filled with detached frame dwellings of two to three storeys on narrow deep lots, with stables and sheds behind. Raymond & Co., manufacturers of medicinal plasters, stands on East 2nd Street, and a boarding house lies in the block behind; the Temple Baptist Church, a brick building, sits between East 2nd and East 3rd Streets. Small shops, a paint shop and a hen house appear toward Richmond. The tracks run diagonally down the right side, and Cottage Place follows their west edge as a narrow street with lots only on its west side. At the bottom right, beyond the tracks, a short stretch of East 4th Street has the Standard Oil Co. storage, The Baird Co. surgical instrument factory with a coal shed and a few dwellings. A north arrow and compass rose occupy the open ground at the right. North Avenue is lettered at the top beside Richmond. Block numbers 117 to 119 and 218 are printed. Adjoining sheets are 6, 8, 3, 13, 14 and 52.
notes: Washington is the street now called Roosevelt Avenue.
Modern East 2nd Street lies about 6 to 8 m from the drawn street and was left out of the fit as displaced.

Roosevelt Avenue is drawn only about 35 ft wide here against 82 ft in the parcels; street_widths 36 was set. Railroad crossings were left out of the fit (use_railroads false) because the drawn tracks differ from the modern line.
Map, 50 ft. E 2nd, E 3rd, Cottage Pl, E 4th, North Av, Washington (Roosevelt Av, drawn 36 ft). One part; East 2nd St left out.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the residential blocks of east Plainfield between Richmond at the top and Washington at the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The Central Railroad of New Jersey right of way, drawn with many parallel tracks, cuts the upper left corner, and East 4th Street runs along its east edge. East 5th, East 6th and East 7th Streets run down the page, crossed in the middle by Franklin Place, which divides the sheet into an upper and a lower tier of blocks. The blocks are built with rows of two to three storey frame dwellings, some of brick or brick veneer, on deep lots. The Bryant Public School, a large brick building heated and lighted from its own plant, stands in the upper block between East 5th and East 6th Streets. At the upper left, along East 4th Street near Richmond, are the Salvation Army building, a stone cutting shop and a gas engine house. Bethel Chapel (Presbyterian) stands at the foot of the block between East 5th and East 6th Streets near Washington, and the Wetumpka Inn is in the lower block east of East 6th Street. A fire alarm box stands at East 5th Street and Franklin Place. Block numbers 219 to 223 are printed. The sheet adjoins sheet 7 on the left, sheets 2 and 56 on the right, sheet 3 above and sheet 14 below.
notes: Washington is the street now called Roosevelt Avenue; Roosevelt Avenue is drawn about 35 ft wide here (street_widths 36).
The drawn tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey differ from the modern Raritan Valley Line; rail crossings were not used.
Map, 50 ft. E 4th to E 7th, Franklin Pl, Washington (Roosevelt Av). One part.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers a strip of central Plainfield along the Green Brook, the boundary between the City of Plainfield (Union County) and the Borough of North Plainfield (Somerset County). The sheet lies between Chatham Street at the top and East Front Street at the bottom, and between Somerset Street on the left and Watchung Avenue on the right. The upper part holds the blocks along Pearl and Warren Streets: dwellings, stables and outbuildings, a livery and blacksmith, a wagon house, a cement block and undertaker's shop, a bottling works and wholesale liquor store, and Debeles Hall, a stage hall with stores and electric light rooms. Pearl Street divides these from the lower block, where large lots of dwellings, barns and a milk depot lie north of the brook. Green Brook crosses the middle of the sheet with the Mill Race beside it; both are drawn in blue. Along East Front Street the lower edge of the sheet is a continuous row of brick and frame business buildings: furniture, clothing and photograph shops, offices, a bank, paint and oil, hardware, a large department store and business college, and at the right the Y.M.C.A. building with its gymnasium and auditorium. Along Somerset Street are a carriage and auto factory with garage and repository, a flour, grain and hay mill with a turbine wheel, and a laundry. Water pipes and overhead lines (O.H.) are marked in the streets, with fire alarm boxes at several corners. Neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins: 10 above, 18 and 23 to the left, 12 to the right, and 15 and 24 below. The scale bar is 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Chatham Street is Brook Avenue north of Watchung Avenue today; the modern node Brook Avenue / Chatham Street / Watchung Avenue falls on this sheet.
The Front Street / Park Avenue / Somerset Street junction is one modern node about 25 m from where the sheet draws Park Av. meeting E. Front St.
Map, 50 ft. Green Brook and mill race between Chatham, Pearl, Warren, Watchung Av, E Front, Somerset; Y.M.C.A. One part. Borders north-plainfield-1910.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 lies immediately east of sheet 11 and shows Boice's Pond and the Green Brook on the boundary between the City of Plainfield (Union County) and the Borough of North Plainfield (Somerset County). The sheet is bounded by Chatham Street and Brook Avenue along the top, Watchung Avenue on the left, East Front Street at the bottom and Elm Place on the right. The brook enters at the upper right, widens into Boice's Pond across the centre of the sheet, and leaves at the left through a culvert under Watchung Avenue; a Mill Race branches off near the bottom left. The compass rose stands in the middle of the pond. In the upper left, between Chatham Street, Pearl Street and Watchung Avenue, are rows of dwellings, and the Watchung Silk Co. broad silk mill (not running June 1910) with its engine and boiler rooms. Along the top right a row of eight dwellings fronts Chatham Street. On the south shore stand Tier's ice houses and ice cream factory with an adjoining pavilion and parlor, and a gospel meeting room and dwellings on Bank Place and East Front Street. The First Presbyterian Church, brick with Sunday school and its own heating and lighting plant, stands on a block between the pond and East Front Street, and frame dwellings line Elm Place on the east shore. Water pipes of 6 and 16 inch bore are marked in the streets. The neighbouring sheets are numbered on the margins: 9 above, 11 to the left, 13 below, and 5 and 6 to the right. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Chatham Street east of Watchung Avenue is Brook Avenue today; the sheet prints both Chatham and Brook Av.
Bank Place survives only as a service way in OpenStreetMap, not as a named street.
Map, 50 ft. Boice's Pond and Green Brook, Watchung Silk Co.; Brook Av/Chatham, Pearl, Elm Pl, Bank Pl, E Front, Church, Washington. One part.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 shows four blocks of central Plainfield east of Watchung Avenue, between East Front Street at the top and East 3rd Street at the bottom, divided by Church Street in the middle and Washington Street on the right. East 2nd Street crosses the sheet between the upper and lower rows of blocks. The upper left block holds the Y.W.C.A. building and a boarding house, a gymnasium, a cabinet maker's and upholsterer's shop, plumbing and tinning works, a fireproof concrete building, a blacksmith and dwellings. The upper right block along East Front Street has a long row of brick dwellings, boarding houses, dwellings, a china and glass packing shop and a plumber. Below East 2nd Street the left block is occupied by the glasshouses and work room of Carl Petersen, florist, and by the Meeting House of the Religious Society of Friends, dated 1788, standing among dwellings. The lower right block holds W. E. Bartle's stone yard with its rubbing, planing and sawing mill, a wagon house and stables, a paint shop and dwellings. At the bottom the tracks of the C. R. R. of N. J. cross the sheet diagonally, with the Union Beef Co. and Swift & Co. meat and provisions plants on their north side along East 3rd Street. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the left margin. Sheets 12 and 6 adjoin above, 15 and 16 to the left, 6 and 7 to the right and 14 below. Water pipes and overhead lines are marked in the streets. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Church Street is drawn 33 ft wide against about 79 ft today, and its modern centreline sits about 3 m off the drawn one, so its junctions were left out of the control.
Washington Street is Roosevelt Avenue today; Church Street survives as Church Street.
Bank Place at the top margin (see sheet 12) survives only as a service way in OpenStreetMap.
Map, 50 ft. E Front to E 3rd between Watchung and Washington; Church St drawn 33 ft (left out); CRR at bottom. One part.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 shows the blocks east of Watchung Avenue and south of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, between Church Street at the top and East 7th Street at the bottom, with Washington Street along the right edge. The railroad's tracks cross the top of the sheet diagonally; a dilapidated structure and a shed stand beside them. The upper block is the works of the Public Service Gas Co., with gas holders, an oil tank, a wagon shed, a meter room, a purifying house, a coal shed beside the tracks and an office; west of Church Street stands the large Nat Levy & Co. factory making ladies' muslin underwear, with stock rooms, an office, a laundry and upholstery and cabinet making, and a large gas holder. Below East 4th Street the next block holds the L. C. Van Nest sash, blinds and doors works with cement block and moulding departments, among rows of dwellings; the blocks along East 5th Street, East 6th Street and East 7th Street are almost wholly dwellings, with a brick-fronted house, stores and a livery at the Watchung Avenue corners. At the lower left Watchung Avenue is drawn with an oval turn-around beside a fire alarm box. A compass rose stands at the right. The drawn Washington Street is only 33 feet wide. Water pipes and overhead lines are marked in the streets. Adjoining sheets are 13 above, 16 and 17 to the left, 7 and 8 to the right and 56 below. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: The street printed East 4th Street between Watchung Avenue and Washington is Court Place near Watchung Avenue today; East 4th Street meets Roosevelt Avenue only at the right-hand end.
Washington Street is Roosevelt Avenue today and is drawn 33 ft wide.
A second East 4th Street label stands at the left margin, west of Watchung Avenue, at the junction the modern data places as East 4th Street / Watchung Avenue.
Map, 50 ft. E 4th to E 7th between Watchung and Washington; Public Service Gas Co. One part.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the central business blocks of Plainfield, between Watchung Avenue at the top and Park Avenue at the bottom. East Front Street bounds the sheet on the left, and North Avenue runs diagonally down the right side. East 2nd Street divides the sheet into a left and a right block. The buildings are mostly brick business blocks, stores with offices or halls above, drawn in pink. On the left block along East Front Street stand the Hotel Waldorf with its bar and pool room, a bank with offices above, a livery, bowling alleys with a lodge room, a cafe, a dry cleaning shop, and the Hotel Iroquois at the corner of Park Avenue. Inside the block are the Salvation Army Hall, a cement block construction works, a wagon shed, and the Headquarters of the Plainfield Fire Department, with a table listing its apparatus and crew. The right block holds the Plainfield Cab Co. and a boarding stable, City Offices, the City Market, the Daily Press, a Chinese laundry, the Hotel Kensington, a dining room and several tin shops, paint and oil stores and offices, packed along the slanting North Avenue front. A compass rose stands at the upper right. Streets are labelled with their widths and the 6 and 8 inch water pipes, with fire alarm boxes at several corners. Adjoining sheets are 13 above, 11 and 24 to the left and below, 25 below right, and 16 to the right. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: The Front Street / Park Avenue / Somerset Street junction is one modern node near Somerset Street and Front Street; the sheet draws Park Av. meeting E. Front St. about 25 m from it, so the node fixes the Somerset Street end only.
North Avenue / Watchung Avenue at the upper right is not found by the detector; the street ends near the sheet edge.
Map, 50 ft. Downtown: E Front, Watchung, E 2nd, North Av, Park Av; brick business blocks. One part.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 shows the area south-east of Plainfield's business centre, between Watchung Avenue at the top and Park Avenue at the bottom. North Avenue runs diagonally along the left edge and E. 5th St. along the right. The tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, ten or more lines wide, run diagonally from the top to the bottom of the sheet, with the West Bound and East Bound waiting rooms (the latter on a long platform) joined by a tunnel. Along North Avenue, a continuous row of brick stores and offices between the avenue and the tracks includes a pool room, printing office, tin shop and hall. East of the tracks lie large undivided blocks: the Brokaw auto garage and cement block works (C. B. Brokaw Auto. Co.), a printing office and machine shop, a steam laundry, and, in the lower middle, the N. Y. Telephone Co. store house and the Telephone Building of fireproof construction. On the right, between Sycamore and Watchung Avenue, stand the Wm. T. Kirk Co. iron works, a machine shop and dwellings; between Sycamore and Park Avenue stand the Police Station with its cells, garages of cement blocks, a repair shop, a livery, carriage houses, a wholesale grocery, a cycle repairing shop, drug stores and dwellings. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the top. Fire alarm boxes, water pipes and overhead lines are shown in the streets. Adjoining sheets are 13 and 14 above, 15 to the left, 25 and 26 below and 17 to the right. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: The street printed E. 4th St. between the tracks and Sycamore (at the upper right) is Court Place near Watchung Avenue today; the E. 4th St. further left is East 4th Street.
Sycamore is lettered across the middle of the right block without a suffix; no modern Sycamore Street fits its position in the street extract.
The rail corridor is drawn about where the Raritan Valley Line stands, but North Avenue / Watchung Avenue at the top left was not detected.
Map, 50 ft. North Av, CRR tracks and stations, Watchung, E 3rd to E 5th, Park Av. One part.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 shows a residential district of Plainfield south-east of the downtown, between Watchung Avenue at the top and Park Avenue at the bottom, from East 5th Street on the left to East 7th Street and a slanting line of Crescent Avenue on the right. Sycamore crosses the middle of the sheet and divides the district into four large blocks, with East 6th Street running between the left and right pairs. The blocks are almost entirely frame dwellings, many of two and a half storeys with outbuildings, with a small number of garages and storage sheds. A few trades appear at the upper left corner on Watchung Avenue: a drug store and stores in a brick row, a tin shop and a hollow tile works. The Hermitage, a dwelling with dining rooms, stands in the block below. The right block between Sycamore and Park Avenue holds Grace Church (Protestant Episcopal), drawn in blue with its parish house and a 50 foot tower, both heated by hot water and lit by gas and electricity; The Plainfield Boarding and dental offices occupy houses along Park Avenue in the left block. At the top right, Watchung Avenue is drawn forking around an oval grassed island, with Crescent Avenue leaving it to the right. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the right edge. Water pipes and overhead lines are shown in the streets and widths are marked of 50 and 33 feet. Adjoining sheets are 14 above, 16 to the left, 26 and 27 below, and 56 to the right. Drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Sycamore is printed without a suffix; it crosses the sheet between the E. 5th St., E. 6th St. and E. 7th St. blocks. No Sycamore Street appears in the street extract at this position.
East 7th Street / Watchung Avenue at the upper right was not detected, since Watchung Avenue is drawn curving around an oval island there.
Map, 50 ft. Watchung to Park, E 5th to E 7th, Sycamore, Grace Church. One part.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 covers the centre of Plainfield's downtown along West Front Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It spans from Somerset Street at the top to Grove Street at the bottom, between Craig Place on the left and West Front Street on the right. Green Brook runs down the middle of the sheet and is lettered as the boundary between the Borough of North Plainfield on the left and the City of Plainfield on the right; two bridges carry Somerset Street and Grove Street across it and a third carries Madison Avenue. North of Madison Avenue, the Front Street side is built solid with brick commercial blocks: Proctors Theatre, the American Sabbath Tract Society printing house, the Babcock Building with its offices and post office, a bakery, a bottling works, furniture and drug stores, a bank and the Farmers Hotel, with wagon and hotel sheds behind. Along Somerset Street east of the brook stands a row of stores and a saloon. West of the brook the blocks facing Craig Place are lined with detached frame dwellings on deep lots, together with a church and the Young Mens Hebrew Assn. building. South of Madison Avenue stand The New Madison Apartments, the Schiller Bros. underwear works and a row of Front Street stores. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets. The adjoining sheets are numbered 11 (above), 18 (left), 24 (right) and 32 (below).
notes: Somerset Street, Park Avenue and West Front Street meet at one modern node; the sheet draws Park Avenue about 120 ft north of Somerset Street.
Pearl Street (north) and Craig Place (south) are drawn as one straight street; Duer is the west part of Madison Avenue, west of Green Brook.
Drawn building labels include Proctors Theatre, American Sabbath Tract Society Printing, Babcock Building, The New Madison Apartments, Dutch Reformed Church.
Map, 50 ft. Somerset to Grove between Craig Pl and W Front; Green Brook; Proctors Theatre. One part.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 shows the district around the Central Railroad of New Jersey line through Plainfield, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The sheet runs from Park Avenue at the top to Central Avenue at the bottom and from West 2nd Street at the left to West 4th Street at the right, crossed by Arlington Avenue and Madison Avenue. The multi-track railroad, lettered C. R. R. of N. J., runs diagonally up the middle of the sheet, with a trestle and coal pockets beside it. Along it stand the lumber and coal yards of Boice, Runyon Co., Wadley & Goodenough, Vanzandt & Voorhees and the Plainfield Ice & Supply Co., a coal and ice plant of the Crystal Ice & Coal Co., and, near the bottom, a large lumber and machine works marked as the Spicer Mfg. Co. with its sprinkler notes printed in the margin. On West 2nd Street the Public Service Electric Co. station occupies a large block, with a lamp department beside it. Park Avenue at the top is lined with commercial buildings, among them the Stirling building, the Frost Bldg., the offices of the Courier News and, on the east side of the tracks, the F. L. C. Martin Auto Company, a garage and machine shop. Between the railroad and West 4th Street the blocks hold frame dwellings and a few stables, and a row of attached houses faces Arlington Avenue. Blocks 402 to 407 are numbered. The adjoining sheets are 15 and 16 (above), 24 (left), 26 (right), and 29 and 32 (below).
notes: West 3rd Street jogs at Madison Avenue; the modern streets match the drawn jog.
Drawn railroad: Central Railroad of New Jersey (modern Raritan Valley Line); drawn tracks lie about 4 m from the modern line.
Park Avenue is drawn 53 ft wide; Madison Avenue 50 ft, drawn narrower (about 34 ft between edges) at West 2nd Street.
Map, 50 ft. Park to Central, W 2nd to W 4th; CRR through the middle; lumber and coal yards. One part.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 shows a residential district of the City of Plainfield west of the business centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left. It covers two columns of blocks between West 4th Street on the left and West 6th Street on the right, divided by West 5th Street, from Park Avenue at the top to Central Avenue at the bottom, crossed by Arlington Avenue and Madison Avenue. Most lots hold detached frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys, many with rear stables or auto houses, set on deep lots along the avenues and the numbered streets. The block between West 4th and West 5th Streets south of Arlington Avenue is largely given to public schools: the Franklin School on West 4th Street and the Stillman School beside it, joined by a yard that runs through the block. Across West 5th Street, at the corner of Madison Avenue, stands the Whittier Public School, and on the same block near Central Avenue is the Seventh Day Baptist Church of Christ, a stone building. A livery stable stands near Park Avenue on the block between West 5th and West 6th Streets. A few brick and brick-veneered houses are mixed with the frame dwellings. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along every street, and block numbers (300, 301, 309, 310, 311, 312) are printed in the blocks. The sheet adjoins sheets 16 and 17 above, 25 to the left, 27 to the right and 29 and 30 below.
notes: Pilot sheet of the atlas: 12 detected junctions.
Schools named: Franklin School, Stillman School, Whittier Public School; church: Seventh Day Baptist Church of Christ.
Map, 50 ft (pilot). Park Av to Central Av between W 4th St and W 6th St; Franklin, Stillman and Whittier schools. One part.

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 shows a residential district of Plainfield west of the centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It is a regular grid of six large blocks between West 6th Street on the left, West 7th Street in the middle and West 8th Street on the right, and between Park Avenue at the top and Central Avenue at the bottom, divided by Arlington Avenue and Madison Avenue. The blocks are deep and thinly built, mostly detached frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys with a few brick-veneered houses, carriage houses and small auto houses. Institutions are scattered among them: the Truell Inn, a family hotel with a tower, at the corner of Park Avenue and College Place; All Souls Church (Unitarian), a private school and the Plainfield Seminary in the block north of Arlington Avenue; the Hartridge School (private) with its auditorium and the Cong'l Church in the block between Arlington and Madison Avenues. A scale bar is printed in Madison Avenue at the left. Water pipes are marked in every street, and block numbers 302, 303, 307, 308, 313 and 314 are printed in the blocks. The sheet is bordered by sheets 17 (above left), 56 (above right), 26 (left), 28 (right) and 30 (below).
notes: Park Avenue is labelled 53 ft wide west of West 7th Street and 60 ft east of it.
Hartridge School and Plainfield Seminary are private schools; Truell Inn is lettered Family Hotel.
The Arlington Avenue / West 6th Street junction was detected 11 m from the modern node and rejected; the remaining 10 junctions fit to 0.65 m.
Map, 50 ft. W 6th to W 8th, Park to Central; Plainfield Seminary, Hartridge School. One part.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 shows a residential strip of Plainfield west of the centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It covers four blocks between West 8th Street on the left and West 9th Street on the right, from Park Avenue at the top to Central Avenue at the bottom, crossed by College Place, Arlington Avenue and Madison Avenue. The block between Park Avenue and College Place holds the Job Male Public Library, a pink-shaded building with a tower, beside rows of detached frame dwellings. South of College Place a whole block is an open park (lettered Park, block 305), drawn with no buildings. The blocks between Arlington and Madison Avenues and between Madison and Central Avenues contain detached dwellings of two to three storeys, a few with brick fronts, with carriage houses, auto houses and sheds. Water pipes are marked in the streets, and block numbers 304, 305, 306 and 315 are printed. The right side of the sheet, beyond West 9th Street, is blank, and the margin holds a north arrow, a scale bar and the sheet number. Adjoining sheets are 27 (left), 56 (above and below) and 59 (right).
notes: Job Male Public Library stands on Park Avenue at West 8th Street.
The mapped area is a narrow strip; the area to the right of West 9th Street is blank margin.
Map, 50 ft. W 8th to W 9th, Park to Central, College Pl; Job Male Public Library. One part.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 shows a residential and light-industrial district of Plainfield west of the centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the upper right. Its top edge is the Central Railroad of New Jersey, lettered C. R. R. of N. J., whose many tracks cross the upper part of the sheet diagonally and pass under a steel bridge at the top right; a coal and wood yard (R. L. Cline) with coal pockets and a few small dwellings and sheds lie just south of the tracks. Below them three east-west streets, West 3rd, West 4th and West 5th Streets, are crossed by Liberty Street at the left, New Street in the middle and Central Avenue at the right; Division runs south from West 5th Street. The blocks are filled with detached frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys, a few in brick, with stables, auto houses and sheds. Named buildings include St. Mary's T.A.B. Assn. hall, the Truell Court Family Hotel (a large building with a dining room and kitchen, heated by steam and lit by electricity), S. C. Baker & Son printing works and the row of dwellings at the corner of West 4th Street and New Street. Block numbers 413 to 416 and 318 to 325 are printed in the blocks. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in each street, and a scale bar and compass are drawn in the margins. The adjoining sheets are 32 (above), 35 and 36 (left), 25 and 26 (right) and 30 (below).
notes: Division is probably the modern Field Avenue (the detector matched Field Avenue / West 5th Street at 0.06 m).
Drawn railroad: Central Railroad of New Jersey (modern Raritan Valley Line); the sheet is turned about 90 degrees from sheets 25 to 28.
Map, 50 ft, north upper right. W 3rd to W 5th, Liberty, Division (today Field Av), New, Central. One part.

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 shows a residential district of Plainfield west of the centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the upper right. It lies south of sheet 29 and covers the blocks between Liberty Street at the left, Division and New Street in the middle, and Central Avenue at the right, from West 6th Street at the top to West 8th Street at the bottom, with West 7th Street between. Most lots hold detached frame dwellings of two to three storeys, with a few brick or brick-veneered houses, carriage houses and small auto houses; the lower blocks have large houses set on deep grounds. In the upper left block stand St. Mary's Convent (marked as built from plans) and an assembly room; the Swedish Evang'l Cong'l Pilgrim Church, with a 28 ft tower, is at the corner of New Street and West 6th Street. Block numbers 316 to 325 are printed. Water pipes (6 and 12 inch) and hydrants are marked along each street, and a compass and scale bar appear in the margins. The adjoining sheets are 29 (above), 36 and 61 (left), 26 and 27 (right) and 56 (below).
notes: Division is probably the modern Field Avenue (Field Avenue / West 7th Street and / West 6th Street fit to 0.7 m and 0.2 m).
The sheet is turned about 90 degrees from sheets 25 to 28, as is sheet 29.
Map, 50 ft, north upper right. W 6th to W 8th, Liberty, Division (Field Av), New, Central. One part.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers the west end of West Front Street in Plainfield and the valley of Green Brook, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies toward the upper right. Green Brook, lettered as the boundary between the Borough of North Plainfield (above) and the City of Plainfield (below), winds across the top of the sheet in a blue channel. Below it, Sycamore Avenue curves down from the brook to West Front Street, which crosses the middle of the sheet. South of West Front Street the sheet shows the blocks between Plainfield Avenue at the left, Elmwood Place and Liberty Street, down to West 2nd Street at the bottom, where the Central R. R. of N. J. is lettered along the edge. The district is mostly detached frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys on deep lots, with a few brick-fronted houses, carriage houses, sheds and auto houses. The Crescent Embossing Co., a two- and three-storey works with its own dynamo and fire-protection notes, stands in the block west of Elmwood Place; the Park Club, a brick building, occupies the top right corner, and a stone cutter's shop is marked on the Front Street frontage. Orchard Place enters Liberty Street from the right. Block numbers 420 to 423 are printed. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in the streets. The adjoining sheets are 49 (above), 33 (left), 54 and 32 (right) and 35 (below).
notes: Washington Avenue is lettered at the right edge of the sheet, split between WASHINGTON and AV.; confidence medium.
The Plainfield Avenue / West Front Street junction lies about 160 px off the left edge of the image; its position is extrapolated.
Fitted rotation is about 39 degrees, about 10 degrees less than sheets 29 and 30.
Map, 50 ft. Green Brook, Sycamore Av, W Front, Plainfield Av, Elmwood Pl, Liberty, W 2nd. One part.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 shows part of the City of Plainfield and the adjoining Borough of North Plainfield around the crossing of Green Brook, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Washington Avenue runs down the left side and Grove Street and Central Avenue down the right, with Prospect Place along the top, West Front Street across the middle and West 2nd Street along the bottom. Green Brook crosses the upper half from left to right in a heavy double line, passing under a bridge on Washington Avenue and another on Grove Street; the sheet notes that the ground north of the brook lies in North Plainfield, Somerset County, and the ground south of it in Plainfield, Union County. North of the brook, a block of dwellings fronts Prospect Place, and a long row of attached frame dwellings with stores stands along Grove Street. South of the brook, the Rosenthal Brothers' Berfelden Mills, broad silk weavers, occupy a brick building with a note on watchman, heating and fire protection; the First Baptist Church (shown in blue) stands at the corner of Grove Street and West Front Street. Below West Front Street lie residential blocks with the Leal School (private), the City Granite Works, the Congregation Children of Israel synagogue, The Bristol with second-hand furniture, and, at the lower right, the Eastern Bottling Company bottling works. Orchard Place and New Street cross the lower blocks. Block numbers 53, 410, 411, 417, 418 and 419 are printed in the blocks, with the adjoining sheets 18, 23, 24, 25, 29 and 31 named at the edges.
notes: Grove Street meets Central Avenue and West Front Street at one modern node.
New Street is drawn about 40 ft wide and its modern line is 4 to 7 m off the drawn one: it was left out of the control points.
The brook crossing on Grove Street is labelled Bridge; the sheet title box names Plainfield and Union County with North Plainfield and Somerset County.
Map, 50 ft. Washington Av at Green Brook, North Plainfield boundary; New St left out (displaced 4-7 m). One part.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 shows the southwest edge of the built-up part of Plainfield along West Front Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Green Brook runs along the top, between the Borough of North Plainfield and the City of Plainfield, and is crossed by a steel bridge on Geraud Avenue. West Front Street runs across the middle of the sheet and Plainfield Avenue down the right edge. Most of the ground between the brook and West Front Street is open land in large blocks (431, 421), with a few outbuildings near the left edge and a dwelling and greenhouse on the right. South of West Front Street, Lafayette Place and Waynewood Place run south, the latter ending in a circular turning bay, and the large block 428 holds a few dwellings, a greenhouse and sheds; a row of dwellings fronts Plainfield Avenue on the right. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet from left to right on a wide embankment with several tracks, and below it a row of small dwellings fronts South 2nd Street, with the Watchung Stone Company's yard, platform and hydrated lime and cement building and a siding. Block numbers 428, 429, 431, 433 and 421 are printed, and the adjoining sheets 31, 34, 35, 37 and 49 are named at the edges.
notes: Waynewood Place is Waynewood Park in OpenStreetMap.

Control rests on four junctions along West Front Street and one at the sheet edge (Plainfield Avenue and South 2nd Street); the rotation of this part is poorly fixed and was not checked against the adjoining sheets.
The steel bridge over Green Brook on Geraud Avenue is labelled Steel Bridge.
Map, 50 ft. W Front, Geraud Av, Plainfield Av, Lafayette Pl, Waynewood Pl (Waynewood Park). One part; 4 of 5 points on W Front (low).

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 shows the western edge of Plainfield along West Front Street and the Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. West Front Street runs down the left third of the sheet with a long row of dwellings along its east side, and West End Avenue crosses the bottom left, where Grant Avenue starts. Lafayette Place and Oxford Place cross the upper middle, with small blocks of detached dwellings between them. A wide corridor of railroad tracks on the Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the lower half from top to bottom and passes under Grant Avenue on a steel bridge. East of the tracks stand industrial works along South 2nd Street: the Potter Printing Press Company, with foundry, pattern house, pattern shop, machine shops, stock room and office, occupying a long pink brick building with raised skylights; the Commercial Mills and Elevator with a coal and wood yard, coal pockets and a wagon shed; and a hay and feed store. The George O. Stevens coal and wood yard with a large coal trestle and pockets lies between West Front Street and the tracks near the bottom. A large part of the left side is open land in block 431. Block numbers 430, 431, 432 and 433 are printed, and the adjoining sheets 33, 37, 39, 45 and 48 are named.
notes: The junction of South 2nd Street with Muhlenberg Place at the right edge was not detected and is not in the control points.
Control is four points, three of them along West Front Street; medium confidence.
Map, 50 ft. W Front, Lafayette, Oxford Pl, West End Av, Grant Av; Potter Printing Press works on the CRR. One part.

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 shows a residential district of Plainfield west of the railroad, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Liberty Street runs along the top and Plainfield Avenue across the lower middle, with West 3rd Street and West 4th Street running down the sheet between them; South 2nd Street runs obliquely along the left side beside the wide corridor of tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, and West 2nd Street, Elmwood Place and a dashed water-pipe line lie to its west. Most lots hold detached frame dwellings, two to two and a half storeys, with stables and sheds behind; the block north of Plainfield Avenue between South 2nd Street and West 3rd Street carries the Mt. Olive Baptist Church, with a parsonage, near Liberty Street, and brick stores and shops along Liberty Street on the next block, including a bakery, a pool room and a restaurant. The Shiloh Baptist Church and the Mt. Zion A.M.E. Church stand on the block between West 3rd and West 4th Streets, and brick stores stand at the corners on Liberty Street. The blocks south of Plainfield Avenue are lighter built, and the Baptist Cemetery fills the lower right corner. Block numbers 424, 425, 326, 427, 426 and 346 are printed, and the adjoining sheets 29, 31, 33, 36, 37 and 38 are named at the edges.
notes: The Liberty Street and West 2nd Street junction at the top left was measured on narrow street edges (3 m residual) and rests on the railroad corridor margin.
Map, 50 ft. Liberty to Plainfield Av, W 2nd to W 4th. One part.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 shows a residential district of Plainfield, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Liberty Street runs along the top and Plainfield Avenue along the bottom, with West 5th, West 6th and West 7th Streets running down the sheet between them, three columns of blocks (326, 327, 328). The middle block is occupied by St. Mary's Roman Catholic Church, a large brick building with heating boiler and a rectory attached, and St. Marys School, a brick building with a furnace, heated and lighted by electricity, on West 5th Street; a second St. Marys School, a brick building heated by steam and lighted by gas and electricity, stands at the top of the next block on West 6th Street. The rest of the blocks hold detached frame dwellings of two and three storeys, some brick, with storage buildings and auto houses behind, set on deep lots; the right block on West 7th Street has some large dwellings of three storeys. South of Plainfield Avenue the ground is largely taken by the Baptist Cemetery and the Methodist Cemetery (block 346), with a few dwellings on the right edge along a street running southwest. Block numbers 29, 30 and 61 and adjoining sheets 35, 37 and 38 are named at the edges.
notes: St. Mary's Church and School are printed as St. Marys R.C. Church and St. Marys School.
Map, 50 ft. Liberty, W 5th to W 7th, Plainfield Av; St Mary's church and schools. One part.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 shows a residential district of Plainfield south of Plainfield Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. South 2nd Street runs down the left side, West 3rd Street and West 4th Street run down the middle and right, and Spooner Avenue crosses the bottom; John Street meets West 4th Street at the right edge. Muhlenberg Place curves across the lower left from South 2nd Street towards West 3rd Street, leaving a small triangular block of dwellings between them near Spooner Avenue. Almost all the buildings are detached frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys, with sheds behind; in the upper left a large block between South 2nd Street and Muhlenberg Place is largely open, with a few dwellings and a long dwelling row near the lower left; Hope Chapel, with a gymnasium and a bowling alley, stands on West 4th Street near the top of the right-hand block, which is lined with dwellings on both sides of the street. A firebox and water mains are marked along the streets. Block numbers 426, 427, 434 and 83 appear, and the adjoining sheets 33, 34, 35, 38 and 39 are named at the edges.
notes: Only three junctions fixed this part (John Street at West 4th Street, and Spooner Avenue at West 3rd and West 4th Streets); low confidence.
The drawn Spooner Avenue and South 2nd Street junction sits about 6 m from its modern node and was not used; the Muhlenberg Place junctions were not detected.
Map, 50 ft. S 2nd, Muhlenberg Pl, W 3rd, W 4th, John, Spooner Av. One part; three points only (low).

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 shows a residential district of Plainfield south of John Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. John Street runs across the upper middle, Spooner Avenue along the bottom, and West 4th Street, Essex Street and West 7th Street run down the sheet; Spruce Street crosses the middle between West 4th Street and Essex Street. The top third of the sheet is taken by the Baptist Cemetery and the Methodist Cemetery, which share block 346 and are separated by a vertical line, with a row of dwellings on John Street along their lower edge. Below John Street, blocks 347 and 348 and the blocks between hold detached frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys, mostly set on deep lots, with a few auto houses, carpenter shops and a storage building; the lots between West 4th Street and Essex Street are close together, with rows of small dwellings on Spruce Street. Block numbers 227, 228, 230 and 346 are printed in the blocks, and the adjoining sheets 35, 36, 37, 40 and 61 are named at the edges.
notes: The junctions of Spooner Avenue with West 4th Street and West 7th Street were not detected.
Map, 50 ft. Cemeteries; John, W 4th, Essex, W 7th, Spruce, Spooner. One part.

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 shows a residential district of the City of Plainfield south-west of the business centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Two long blocks run across the sheet between South 2nd Street along the top, West 3rd Street in the middle and West 4th Street along the bottom, bounded on the left by Grant Avenue and on the right by Spooner Avenue. The upper block is numbered 435 and the lower 436. Almost all lots hold detached two and two-and-a-half storey frame dwellings, many set well back on deep lots with small outbuildings, stables and sheds to the rear; a few three-storey buildings stand at the upper left corner on Grant Avenue. The one public building is the pink-tinted Fire Department Hose Company No. 3 on the south side of West 3rd Street, with a note listing its captain, men, horses, combination wagon, chemical tank, hose and supply wagon. Water mains of 6 and 8 inches run in every street, with fire alarm boxes at the Grant Avenue and Spooner Avenue corners and drinking hydrants marked D.H. Street widths of 50, 60 and 66 feet are lettered. Darrow Avenue appears as a short stub south of West 4th Street. The sheet adjoins sheets 34 above, 42 to the left across Grant Avenue, 37 to the right across Spooner Avenue and 40 below. A compass rose, a scale bar and a Princeton University Library stamp are printed in the margins; large parts of the sheet beyond the street frontages are blank.
notes: Fire Department Hose Company No. 3 is on the south side of West 3rd Street.
Modern OpenStreetMap names are the same as the printed ones.
Streets are drawn 50, 60 and 66 feet wide.
Map, 50 ft. S 2nd to W 4th, Grant to Spooner; Hose Co No 3. One part.

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 shows a residential area of the City of Plainfield south of the downtown, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It lies between West 4th Street at the top and West 7th Street at the bottom, and is crossed by Grant Avenue on the left, Darrow Avenue in the middle and Spooner Avenue on the right. The left block, numbered 353, is a large tract with few buildings: scattered two-and-a-half storey dwellings, a coop, auto houses and storage sheds stand on deep, mostly empty lots. East of Darrow Avenue the sheet is more densely built. Along West 4th Street a row of frame dwellings, one marked upholstering, fronts the north side of block 352, and Wallace Place cuts into the block from Spooner Avenue. The pink Washington School stands in the middle of block 352 with a note on its electric motor and fan, steam heat and indirect system, and electric lights. Essex, a street without a suffix, runs between block 352 and block 351 at the right; block 351 holds dwellings, an auto garage, a laundry and storage of plumbing supplies. Streets are lettered 50, 60 and 66 feet wide. Along the left edge are fragments of West 5th Street and West 6th Street as they meet Grant Avenue on the next sheet. The sheet adjoins sheet 39 above, 44 to the left, 38 to the right and 62 below. A compass rose and a scale bar appear on the sheet.
notes: Essex is printed without a suffix; the modern name is Essex Street.
Wallace Place is a short street entering block 352 from Spooner Avenue.
Washington School stands in block 352.
Map, 50 ft. W 4th to W 7th, Grant, Darrow, Spooner; Washington School; Wallace Pl, Essex. One part.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 shows a district of the City of Plainfield south-west of the business centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. South 2nd Street crosses the top of the sheet on a slant, West 3rd Street crosses the middle and West 4th Street the bottom. Monroe Avenue bounds the sheet on the left, and Pond Place, Prescott Place and Stebbins Place cross it from top to bottom. Six blocks are shown, numbered 441 to 445. The blocks along South 2nd Street hold close rows of two-storey and two-and-a-half storey dwellings, many in semi-detached pairs, with deep rear yards given to small outbuildings. Along Stebbins Place the lots are filled with detached frame dwellings, and a pink-tinted double building stands at the corner of West 3rd Street. In the lower left the large Irving Public School, with a note on its steam heat and electric and gas lighting, fronts West 4th Street on Monroe Avenue; a second row of dwellings and outbuildings lies to its right. A club room is noted in block 443. Water mains of 6 and 8 inches run in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes marked. The sheet adjoins sheets 45 above, 63 to the left, 42 to the right and 43 below. A compass rose, a scale bar and a Princeton University Library stamp are printed on it.
notes: Irving Public School stands on West 4th Street at Monroe Avenue.
Modern OpenStreetMap names are the same as the printed ones.
Map, 50 ft. S 2nd to W 4th, Monroe Av to Stebbins Pl; Irving Public School. One part.

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 shows a residential district of the City of Plainfield south-west of the business centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. South 2nd Street runs across the top, West 3rd Street across the middle and West 4th Street along the bottom. Stebbins Place bounds the left side, Lee Place crosses the middle, and Grant Avenue runs down the right edge. Four blocks are numbered 437 to 440. Most lots hold detached two-and-a-half storey frame dwellings, some in semi-detached pairs, with sheds, coops and stables at the rear; the district is more thinly built toward the right, where several large lots are mostly open. Block 438 contains a long storage building and a small fire station marked with a fire motor beside West 3rd Street. A small blue-tinted building stands near the middle of block 439, and a carriage house and an auto house appear in block 437. Water mains of 6 and 8 inches run in West 3rd and West 4th Streets and in Grant Avenue, and street widths of 50 and 66 feet are lettered. The upper part of the sheet is blank, carrying a compass rose and the line of South 2nd Street. It adjoins sheets 45 above, 41 to the left, 39 to the right and 43 and 44 below, and bears a Princeton University Library stamp.
notes: Modern OpenStreetMap names are the same as the printed ones.
The detector found no clear junction of Stebbins Place and West 4th Street on this sheet.
Map, 50 ft. S 2nd to W 4th, Stebbins Pl, Lee Pl, Grant Av. One part.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 shows a residential district of the City of Plainfield south-west of the business centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Three rows of blocks lie between West 4th Street at the top and West 7th Street at the bottom, separated by West 5th and West 6th Streets. Monroe Avenue bounds the left edge. Prescott Place divides the top row at its middle and Lee Place bounds the right edge. The blocks are numbered 357 to 361. The two upper rows are closely built with detached and semi-detached two- and two-and-a-half storey frame dwellings in lines along each street frontage, with small outbuildings at the rear, and a pink-tinted building stands at the corner of Prescott Place and West 4th Street. The lowest block, between West 6th and West 7th Streets, is much more open: a few large dwellings, an auto house, a storage building and a coop stand on deep lots, and the right part of the block is empty. Streets are lettered 50 and 60 feet wide, with 6-inch water mains and fire alarm boxes. Hobart Avenue is lettered on the unmapped area below West 7th Street. At the top, the edge of sheet 42 shows Stebbins Place. The sheet adjoins sheet 41 above, 63 and 64 to the left, 44 to the right and 64 and 62 below. A compass rose and a scale bar are printed on it.
notes: Hobart Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract used as reference.
Lee Place at West 7th Street lies about 19 feet beyond the sheet edge and was not detected.
Map, 50 ft. W 4th to W 7th, Monroe Av, Prescott Pl, Lee Pl. One part.

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 shows a residential district of the City of Plainfield south-west of the business centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Three blocks, numbered 354 to 356, lie between West 4th Street at the top and West 7th Street at the bottom, separated by West 5th and West 6th Streets. Lee Place bounds the left side and Grant Avenue runs down the right side, with the unmapped area beyond it numbered as sheet 40. The upper two blocks are filled with detached two-and-a-half storey frame dwellings in regular rows along the street frontages, with small auto houses, a carriage house and sheds at the rear. The lowest block, between West 6th and West 7th Streets, has a row of dwellings along West 6th Street and only three large houses further south, leaving most of the block open. Water mains of 6 inches run in West 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th Streets and an 8-inch main in Grant Avenue; street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered, and a fire alarm box stands at the upper right. The blocks to the left and top carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets 43 and 42, and sheet 62 lies below. A compass rose and a scale bar are printed on the sheet, which also bears a Princeton University Library stamp.
notes: Modern OpenStreetMap names are the same as the printed ones.
Map, 50 ft. W 4th to W 7th, Lee Pl to Grant Av. One part.

sheet-45-1.description: Sheet 45, part 1, is the left of three vertical strips into which this sheet folds a narrow corridor of southern Plainfield along the Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The strip begins at the top with Grant Avenue crossing South 2nd Street and runs down South 2nd Street to Prescott Place, with the railroad tracks and the heavy line that separates this strip from the next on its right edge. Along the left edge the Central Railroad of New Jersey is marked beside a small branch track, and a one-storey Grant Av. Depot stands near the top. The upper part of the strip is open ground with a few small sheds, a vacant building and a note of fire ruins. Most of the lower part is the long brick machine shop and tool room of The Pond Machine Tool Company, drawn in pink with skylights and automatic sprinklers, with its office, drafting room, blue print room and a blacksmith shop at the bottom. The narrow blocks 42 and 41 lie between South 2nd Street and the railroad, cut by the small lanes Lee Place, Stebbins Place and Prescott Place. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inch bore are marked in the streets, and the north arrow stands on the open ground at the left. The same ground continues in the middle strip (part 2), and sheet 48 is named at the left edge.
notes: The sheet is a corridor folded into three side-by-side strips (parts 1 to 3), each placed separately; the same South 2nd Street is drawn in all three at different points along it.

Placed from Grant Avenue and three hand-picked lane junctions along South 2nd Street (the lanes are not detected): all the points lie on one line, so the fit is a helmert (position, scale and rotation) with no check across the street; medium confidence.
The modern names are the same as the printed ones: Grant Avenue, South 2nd Street, Lee Place, Stebbins Place and Prescott Place.

Map, 50 ft. The South 2nd St / CRR corridor folded into three vertical strips, each a part: 1 Grant Av to Prescott Pl, 2 Prescott Pl to Morris St, 3 at Clinton Av. Placed on hand-picked S 2nd St junctions (helmert) and one anchored point (low).

sheet-45-2.description: Sheet 45, part 2, is the middle of three vertical strips into which this sheet folds a narrow corridor of southern Plainfield along the Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It continues South 2nd Street downhill from the left strip, from Prescott Place at the top past Pond Place, Monroe Avenue and Manson Place to Morris Street, with the heavy line of the railroad on the right edge. Most of the strip is the works of The Pond Machine Tool Company, drawn in pink and yellow: a long foundry and pattern storage on the left, with a pattern shop, wash house, motors, engine room, coal house, machine shop, stock and carpenter shop above, and a core oven, sand and iron floor areas in the middle. A lumber and iron storage shed with a trestle stands beside South 2nd Street, and a switch track and 6 inch water pipe run through the yard. The narrow blocks 41 and 63 on the right of South 2nd Street are cut by the lanes named above, each ending at the tracks, which are drawn as many close parallel lines. The compass rose stands low on the right and a note of the company's fire protection, watchman and sprinkler equipment (Mutual Risk, admittance refused) is printed at the bottom. The same corridor continues in the left strip (part 1) above and the right strip (part 3).
notes: Placed from five hand-picked junctions of South 2nd Street with its lanes (not detected); all lie on one line, so the fit is a helmert with no check across the street. Scale and rotation agree with part 1 to 0.2 percent and 0.1 degree; medium confidence.
The firm's name is printed as The Pond Machine Tool Company (Niles, Bement, Pond Co., Successors).
The modern names are the same as the printed ones.

Map, 50 ft. The South 2nd St / CRR corridor folded into three vertical strips, each a part: 1 Grant Av to Prescott Pl, 2 Prescott Pl to Morris St, 3 at Clinton Av. Placed on hand-picked S 2nd St junctions (helmert) and one anchored point (low).

sheet-45-3.description: Sheet 45, part 3, is the right of three vertical strips into which this sheet folds a narrow corridor of southern Plainfield along the Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The strip shows South 2nd Street on its right edge, running down to Clinton Avenue at the bottom, with the railroad tracks and a heavy dividing line on its left. Most of the strip is one large lot, block 465 (80), mostly open, belonging to The Pond Machine Tool Company. At the top left are the long yellow pattern ware houses and a large reservoir under building, all not sprinklered, and a pattern ware house, with a siding curving past them; across the lot a diagonal part of the company's name is lettered. A block of 63 lies on the other side of South 2nd Street. The scale bar and a library stamp are printed at the bottom, with Clinton Av. lettered along the lower edge, and a fire alarm box and 6 and 8 inch water pipes are marked in the streets. The ground above this strip is in the middle strip (part 2); the sheet below is 46, to which South 2nd Street and Clinton Avenue continue.
notes: Only one street junction (South 2nd Street and Clinton Avenue, at the bottom edge) is on this strip. It is placed by that one measured point and a second point derived from it, with the scale (7.98 px/ft) and rotation of parts 1 and 2; low confidence.
The same junction is also drawn at the top of sheet 46.

Map, 50 ft. The South 2nd St / CRR corridor folded into three vertical strips, each a part: 1 Grant Av to Prescott Pl, 2 Prescott Pl to Morris St, 3 at Clinton Av. Placed on hand-picked S 2nd St junctions (helmert) and one anchored point (low).

sheet-46.description: Sheet 46 lies directly south-west of sheet 45 along the Central Railroad of New Jersey in Plainfield, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Clinton Avenue runs along the top edge, West Front Street runs down the middle of the sheet and South 2nd Street along the right edge, so that the sheet is split into three ground areas. On the left, between Bradford Avenue and West Front Street, are large lots of blocks 475 and 474 with scattered frame dwellings, stables and a vacant hotel at the corner of West Front Street; the lots end in slanting lines at the top. In the middle are the works of the Q.M.S. Company, manufacturers of railroad machine tools: a long machine shop, an engine room and boiler room, a pattern shop with drafting rooms, a blacksmith shop, casting shed, lumber and scrap sheds. A small Clinton Av. Depot stands above them beside the many parallel tracks of the railroad, which run down the middle. On the right is the Manganese Steel Safe Co., manufacturers of safes, with a tall skylighted shop, iron racks, a hot air pan, an engine and dynamo room, a machine shop and a printing shop, and a siding branches off the tracks into the yard. The compass rose stands below the Q.M.S. works. A fire protection note of the Q.M.S. Company is printed over the plant, and De Kalb Avenue crosses the bottom left corner.
notes: Clinton Avenue and De Kalb Avenue are drawn only to their near edges at the top and bottom of the sheet, so their junctions with West Front Street fall off the image. The Clinton Avenue points (West Front Street and South 2nd Street) are hand-picked as the drawn edge plus half the width, with centres outside the image; Bradford Avenue and De Kalb Avenue and Grace Place are measured by the detector. Four points give a first-order fit with a 2.1 m RMSE; low to medium confidence.
Bradford Avenue is Bradford Street today. De Kalb Avenue is Dekalb Avenue. The lane that meets Bradford Avenue and West Front Street is Grace Place today. West Front is West Front Street.
The Q.M.S. Company and the Manganese Steel Safe Co. are named in the sheet's own lettering.
Map, 50 ft. Clinton Av at top, W Front, Bradford Av, De Kalb Av, S 2nd St. One part; two hand-picked points off the image (low).

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 covers the western edge of the City of Plainfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Clinton Avenue runs across the top and South 2nd Street down the left edge, with West 3rd Street, Willever and West 4th Street running down the sheet. Two wide diagonal streets, Evona Avenue and Rushmore Avenue, cut across the middle from the upper left to the lower right, and the dash-dot boundary of the City of Plainfield and Piscataway Township, Middlesex County, crosses them from the lower left to the upper right. The upper right is a built-up area of small frame dwellings, with blocks 453 to 456 around Lyman Place, Astor Place and Hunter Avenue, and the Church of the Heavenly Rest and a chapel at the top right on West 4th Street. West of West 3rd Street the lots lie between View Avenue, Frace Avenue and Leslie Avenue, with many small dwellings in blocks 459 and 458, and a West End Tabernacle stands beside Evona Avenue. The wedge between Evona Avenue and Rushmore Avenue and the ground beyond the boundary are drawn as large open lots. A fire alarm box stands at Clinton Avenue and South 2nd Street at the top left, and sheet 46 and sheet 63 are named at the margins.
notes: Willever is Willever Street today, Frace Avenue is Frace Street, Mabel is Mable Street and Ann is Ann Street.
The fit gives 3.99 px/ft, which is the 100 ft scale (the 50 ft sheets of this atlas fit at about 7.9 px/ft).
Clinton Place is still a short street off Clinton Avenue and was not used as control. Rushmore Avenue / Willever Street was not detected.
Map, 100 ft. Clinton Av, Evona Av, Rushmore Av, W 3rd, W 4th, Willever, Frace Av; Plainfield / Piscataway boundary. One part.

sheet-48-1.description: Sheet 48, part 1, is the upper of two strips drawn one above the other on this sheet along West Front Street in Plainfield, at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. West Front Street runs across the strip with the many parallel tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey below it, and the strip is bounded by Clinton Avenue on the left and Compton Avenue on the right. North of West Front Street the blocks 471, 470, 469 and 468 are cut by Mariners Place and Albert and lined with frame dwellings, some with outbuildings, and the Dunellen Avenue line runs along the top with a row of houses and the Jefferson Public School (fire proof construction, steam heat, gas and electric light) beyond it. South of West Front Street a single block, 466 (206), is lined with dwellings and, at the left, an ice cream and other small works, with the railroad below. A compass rose stands at the right end of the railroad. The heavy line below the tracks is the dividing line with the lower strip (part 2), which continues the ground east of Compton Avenue. Water pipes of 6 inch bore are marked in the streets, and the number 46 is lettered at the left edge, with 45 below.
notes: Dunellen Avenue here is Myrtle Avenue today. Mariners Place, Compton Avenue and Clinton Avenue keep their names; Albert is Albert Street; West Front is West Front Street.
The drawn railroad lies about 20 m from the modern Raritan Valley Line against the street points (the line was elevated about 1900); no rail point was used.
Parts 1 and 2 fit at 3.93 and 3.91 px/ft (100 ft scale) with rotation 40 degrees (north to the upper right).
Map, 100 ft. Two strips along W Front divided by a heavy line: 1 upper (Clinton, Mariners Pl, Dunellen Av = Myrtle Av, Compton), 2 lower (three points only).

sheet-48-2.description: Sheet 48, part 2, is the lower of two strips drawn one above the other on this sheet along West Front Street in Plainfield, at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It continues the street east of Compton Avenue, which runs up the left side to Myrtle Avenue, and runs to Grant Avenue and West End Avenue at the right, where the number 34 is printed at the edge. West Front Street crosses the strip, with the Central Railroad of New Jersey and its many tracks along the bottom and 45 lettered below them. North of West Front Street, in block 467 (207), a row of frame dwellings and outbuildings fronts the street, and houses stand beside West End Avenue; the area above them is left blank except for the Green Brook and its branch Stony Brook, drawn in blue, which cross the middle of the strip with the line of the Borough of North Plainfield and City of Plainfield. South of the street a row of houses stands in block 466 (206) between the street and the railroad. Dunellen Avenue and Myrtle Avenue meet Compton Avenue near the top left, and Myrtle Avenue is drawn as a curve. The compass arrow stands at the upper right.
notes: Dunellen Avenue is the west end of today's Myrtle Avenue; Compton Avenue, Myrtle Avenue, West End Avenue and Grant Avenue keep their names; West Front is West Front Street.

Placed by only three junctions (Compton Avenue / West Front Street, Compton Avenue / Myrtle Avenue, and the Grant Avenue / West End Avenue / West Front Street node), so the fit is exact through them; scale (3.91 px/ft) and rotation (40.4 degrees) agree with part 1; medium confidence.
West End Avenue is only partly drawn near the upper right.
Map, 100 ft. Two strips along W Front divided by a heavy line: 1 upper (Clinton, Mariners Pl, Dunellen Av = Myrtle Av, Compton), 2 lower (three points only).

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 covers a district of the City of Plainfield east of the Green Brook and north of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. East Front runs diagonally down the left side of the sheet and East 2nd Street and Midway run down the middle, crossed by Leland Avenue at the top, Netherwood Avenue, Jackson Avenue, Johnston Avenue and Hill; George runs along the right and St. Mary's Avenue is on the right edge. The sheet is almost entirely residential: blocks 140 to 151 are lined with frame dwellings on narrow lots, many with stables or carriage houses at the rear, with a few small business buildings such as a carriage works, a cement block building, a wash house, a coop and storage sheds. Large open lots lie at the upper left (block 151), in the middle of block 127 and in block 129. A building of a society stands on East 2nd Street and a row of concrete buildings on the west side of block 129. At the bottom right a large block, 130 (201), holds St. Mary's Cemetery, and St. Mary's Place and McKinley Place are short side streets. Fire alarm boxes stand at the corners of Netherwood Avenue and Johnston Avenue, and water pipes of 6 and 10 inch bore are marked in the streets. Sheets 52, 53, 65 and 1 are named at the margins.
notes: Midway is East 3rd Street today. Jackson Avenue is Garfield Avenue today, and St. Mary's Place appears to be St Marks Place; East Front is East Front Street and Mc Kinley Place is McKinley Place.
The fit gives 3.95 px/ft, which is the 100 ft scale; the sheet's scale bar is lettered for 100 feet to an inch.
East Front Street / Leland Avenue falls just off the top of the sheet and was not used as a control point.
Map, 100 ft. Netherwood: Leland, Netherwood, Jackson (Garfield Av), Johnston, Watson, Midway (E 3rd St), St Mary's Pl (St Marks Pl). One part.

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 covers the Green Brook valley on the boundary between the City of Plainfield, Union County, and North Plainfield, Somerset County, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Farragut Road crosses the top edge, Berckman crosses the middle and Norwood Avenue and Richmond cross at the bottom. The Green Brook winds down the left of the sheet in blue, with a pond near the middle of the left side, and the line between the Borough of North Plainfield and the City of Plainfield follows it; Brook Avenue runs down the left edge. East of the brook the large lots of blocks 149 and 126 (146) are mostly open, with scattered frame dwellings and sheds along E. Front, which runs diagonally down the sheet.
