On the right are the long narrow lots of blocks 124 (147) and 123 (148) between East 2nd Street and East 3rd Street, filled with frame dwellings, and blocks 127 (237) and 128 (236) at the top between Midway Avenue and East Front. The Lincoln School stands north of Berckman, and the Plainfield Steam Laundry on East 3rd Street. A row of small houses lines Norwood Avenue at the bottom. A title legend in the upper right names Plainfield and Union County and North Plainfield and Somerset County, and a compass rose is at the top. Sheets 51, 5, 6, 7, 3 and 4 are named in the margins.
notes: Richmond is Richmond Street and Berckman is Berckman Street today; East Front is East Front Street. The sheet's Midway Avenue joins East 3rd Street (Midway is East 3rd Street on sheet 51).
The fit gives 3.97 px/ft, the 100 ft scale, although the printed scale bar reads like a 50 ft bar.
Map, 100 ft (bar looks 50 ft; fit 3.97). Farragut Rd, Brook Av, Norwood, Richmond, Berckman, E Front. One part.

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies toward the upper left. It shows the Netherwood district on the north side of Plainfield, split by the broad double-track embankment of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, which runs from the bottom of the sheet up toward Leland Avenue at the top, with Netherwood Station and a pedestrian crossing beside it. North Avenue follows the west side of the tracks and South Avenue the east side. West of North Avenue lie blocks 133 to 139, cut by Watson, Netherwood, Jackson and Johnston Avenues, with George Street and St. Mary's Avenue at the left edge; the blocks are subdivided into narrow lots with scattered dwellings, and block 137 is entirely vacant. Industry stands along the tracks: the Bias Waterproof Fabric Company with its cement block works, the Century Rubber Trading Company, and Jos. Harrigan's coal, wood, hay and feed yard with its sidings. A pink factory complex with several sheds sits on North Avenue near the bottom. East of the railroad, Fire House No. 4 of the Fire Department is drawn with its note on staffing and equipment, and blocks 259 to 263 hold frame dwellings along South Avenue, Belvidere Avenue, Woodland Avenue and East 7th Street, with St. Stephens Parish House on Woodland Avenue. At the top right a large florist's establishment, Chas. L. Stanley, shows its glass houses. Adjoining sheets 51, 54, 55, 65 and 1 are numbered in the margins.

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies toward the upper left. It covers the hillside residential district east of East 7th Street, which runs down the left edge as a straight street, in the northeast of Plainfield. The streets here are curved and of irregular plan: Belvidere Avenue and Park Terrace sweep around the grounds of Truell Hall, a large institutional building drawn in pink with its note on heating, lighting and fire protection, while Berkeley Avenue, Denmark Road, Dixie Lane, Osborne Avenue and Lorraine curve through large, irregular blocks numbered 264 to 285. Woodland Avenue crosses the lower left diagonally and Ravine Road leads off Belvidere Avenue at the bottom. Straight, narrow-lot subdivision lies at the upper left along Gresham Road and Park Place, between East 7th Street and Berkeley Avenue, with Leland Avenue at the top edge and Helene Avenue at the top right. Houses are mostly dwellings of two and a half storeys on large lots; St. Stephens Episcopal Church with its rectory stands on Woodland Avenue near the bottom, and a blue-coloured building (non-dwelling) appears near the bottom edge. Water pipes run along most streets and the drawn street widths are mostly 50 feet. A compass rose is at the upper left and the scale bar at the lower left. Large parts of blocks 261 and 275 are left open, and sheets 53, 55 and 0 are named at the margins.
notes: Scale 100 feet to an inch; the fitted scale is 3.98 pixels per foot.

sheet-55-1.description: Sheet 55, main part, shows the north-eastern edge of the City of Plainfield, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the right. On the left, Putnam Avenue runs down the sheet and is crossed by Carlton Avenue, Kensington Avenue, Webster Place and Hillside Avenue, with Woodland Avenue at the bottom; these blocks (239, 245, 246) hold rows of frame dwellings on Carlton and Kensington Avenues and a few on Webster Place, with large open lots further south. On the right, a denser grid of narrow lots runs between Scott Avenue, South Avenue, East 6th Street, East 7th Street and Berckman Street, built up with frame dwellings, and Central Avenue crosses diagonally towards the lower right. A brook runs along the top edge. The lower right corner is cut off by a heavy line and holds an inset of the College of Mount St. Mary of the Sisters of Mercy (part 2), which is not part of this ground; sheet 54 adjoins on that side.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch (fitted 3.97 px/ft).
The inset of the College of Mount St. Mary (part 2) lies in Watchung, outside the reference area, with no street drawn; not placed.

sheet-56-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 56 is the larger, eastern part of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It lies east of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, whose double heavy line forms the left edge, and shows the Crescent Avenue district in the north-east of Plainfield. East 7th Street runs from the top of the part to the bottom, with a narrow strip of blocks between it and the railroad carrying Washington Street and Sycamore Street as short stubs. Franklin Place curves along the top right and, with Watchung Avenue, encloses a triangular block of dwellings; below Watchung Avenue the Crescent Avenue Presbyterian Church, drawn in blue, stands at the head of a rounded turning space, and Crescent Avenue curves down the part in a long arc past blocks 207 to 212. East 9th Street runs down the right side, and 1st, 2nd and 3rd Places cross between Crescent Avenue and East 9th Street as short parallel streets lined with small lots. Park Avenue crosses the bottom, with West 7th, West 8th and West 9th Streets meeting it from the south. Houses are nearly all frame dwellings of two or two and a half storeys, many in pink (brick) or yellow (frame). The top right of the part is blank paper belonging to sheet 57, and a compass rose stands there. A second part of the sheet, west of the railroad, is turned differently and is part 2. Numbers of neighbouring sheets (2, 8, 14, 17, 27, 28, 57, 59) appear in the margins.
notes: Sheet 56 holds two separately turned parts divided along the railroad; this is the eastern part, with north toward the upper left (fitted rotation about -26 degrees).
The junction of 3rd Place and East 9th Street was 7 m from its modern node and was rejected from the fit.
The Crescent Avenue Presbyterian Church is lettered as 'Crescent Av. Presbyn Church' on the sheet.
Map, 100 ft. Two parts divided along the CRR: 1 east of the rail (Crescent Av district), 2 west of the rail (Central Av, Stelle Av, Division).

sheet-56-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 56 is the smaller, western part of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top (its own north arrow stands at the left edge). It lies west of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, whose heavy line forms the right edge, and shows the area on both sides of Central Avenue in north-central Plainfield. At the top left West 8th Street runs diagonally up the sheet and meets Central Avenue, which bends down the part from West 9th Street toward the bottom, beside the railroad. A wedge-shaped block (331) bounded by West 8th Street, Division and Central Avenue holds a large pink mansion with outbuildings. Stelle Avenue crosses the part horizontally near the middle, with Field Avenue running down the left edge and Randolph Road across the bottom; the blocks between hold detached frame dwellings on large lots (340 and 389), a few small stables and a stone residence with a blue-coloured wing near the bottom, and a good deal of open ground. Water pipes run along Central Avenue, Stelle Avenue and Field Avenue. Neighbouring sheets 30, 28, 61, 59 and 17 are numbered in the margins. The part is cut from the same scan as part 1, which is turned about 38 degrees from it and lies on the other side of the tracks; the two are separated along the railroad.
notes: Sheet 56 holds two separately turned parts divided along the railroad; this western part has north toward the top (fitted rotation about 12 degrees).
Five of the seven control points rest on a single drawn street edge.
Central Avenue, Stelle Avenue, Field Avenue and Randolph Road keep their names in OpenStreetMap; 'Division' is not found in the extract.
Map, 100 ft. Two parts divided along the CRR: 1 east of the rail (Crescent Av district), 2 west of the rail (Central Av, Stelle Av, Division).

sheet-57.description: Sheet 57 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top. It lies in the north-east of Plainfield between Putnam Avenue at the top and Prospect Avenue at the bottom. Cedar Brook, drawn in blue, enters near Putnam Avenue, flows down through a large open tract (blocks 226 and 235) and crosses Watchung Avenue and Prospect Avenue at the bottom. Franklin Place and East 9th Street form the left side, with a small triangular corner at the bottom left where Park Avenue is cut off; 1st, 2nd and 3rd Places enter from the left as short stubs. Richmond and Carlton Avenues run between Putnam Avenue and Watchung Avenue, lined with small dwellings on narrow lots (blocks 225, 236 and 237); Kensington Avenue forms the right edge, with a column of lots along it, and a larger house and greenhouse stand in block 237 beside Carlton Avenue. Between Watchung Avenue and Prospect Avenue most of the ground is open, with only a few outbuildings and sheds near the brook and a row of houses on Prospect Avenue. East 7th Street appears at the top left as a skewed crossing. A compass rose is at the left and the scale bar at the lower left. Sheets 2, 55, 56, 58, 59 and 60 are named at the margins.
notes: Richmond is 'Richmond Street' in OpenStreetMap.
The junction of 3rd Place and East 9th Street was 9 m from its modern node and was rejected from the fit.
Scale 100 feet to an inch; fitted scale is 3.96 pixels per foot.
Map, 100 ft. Cedar Brook, Putnam to Prospect Av. One part.

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 100 degrees, so that north lies toward the right. It shows the Watchung Avenue district of north-eastern Plainfield. Kensington Avenue runs along the top edge, with Hillside Avenue and Webster Place crossing the upper half; the long streets Prospect Avenue, Highland Avenue, Lake Avenue, Watchung Avenue and Putnam Avenue run down the sheet, Prospect Avenue at the left edge and Putnam Avenue at the right edge. Blocks 247 to 254 hold scattered frame dwellings on long narrow lots, with auto houses and sheds; the large block between Highland Avenue and Watchung Avenue is half empty and block 252 beyond Pine is mostly open ground. Woodland Avenue crosses diagonally from the lower left to Watchung Avenue, a fire alarm box stands at the junction, and Belvidere Avenue curves across the bottom, with Charlotte Road at the lower right and Rahway Road at the lower left. Blocks 267 to 274 at the bottom hold large houses on big grounds, one of them in pink with outbuildings. A compass rose is at the lower left and the scale bar at the bottom. Sheets 57, 55, 60 and 0 are named in the margins.
notes: Turned about 100 degrees from the other sheets; north lies to the right.
Lake Avenue is not found in the OpenStreetMap extract; Pine is 'Pine Street'.
The junction of Kensington Avenue and Putnam Avenue was measured from a narrow pair of lines (Kensington Avenue 31 of 60 ft) and carries a residual of about 4 m.
Map, 100 ft, north to the right. Kensington, Hillside, Highland, Watchung, Pine, Woodland. One part.

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top. It covers the area south-east of the railroad where Park Avenue and Arlington Avenue run diagonally across the part. At the left, Central Avenue and Madison Avenue run down the sheet as parallel streets, crossed by Stelle Avenue and, at the bottom, Randolph Road; the blocks between (332, 333, 338 and 339) are lined with dwellings, and West 9th Street runs up the upper left at a slant to the Plainfield High School, drawn in pink with its grounds and annexes. Union is a narrow street between Madison Avenue and the brook. At the top, Park Avenue and Arlington Avenue run from the school down to the lower right past rows of narrow lots, Arlington Place branches from Park Avenue near the right, and the Park Avenue Baptist Church stands at the top on Park Avenue. Cedar Brook, drawn in blue, cuts through the middle from the top right and runs down a long loop beside block 337 to Randolph Road. Evergreen Avenue, Martine Avenue and Edgewood Avenue lie at the right edge, with Rose at the lower right. A compass rose and scale bar fill the lower right. Sheets 28, 56, 57, 60 and 397 are named at the margins.
notes: Union is the modern Kenyon Avenue; the junctions along it were measured under that name.
Edgewood Avenue is lettered upward along the right edge; the word 'Cedar' of Cedar Brook is partly illegible.
The junction of Evergreen Avenue and Park Avenue lies about 20 m from its modern node and was rejected from the fit.
Scale 100 feet to an inch; fitted scale 3.98 pixels per foot.

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top. It shows a residential district of Plainfield between Prospect Avenue along the top edge and Randolph Road along the bottom, with Hillside Avenue forming the right margin and Edgewood and Arlington Avenues on the left. A series of east-west streets (Evergreen, Martine and Thornton Avenues) is crossed by Edgewood, Kensington and Hillside Avenues to make regular blocks numbered 229 to 234. Park Avenue cuts diagonally from the upper left to the bottom of the sheet, and Arlington Place and Arlington Avenue follow the same angle on the west side, so the blocks there are irregular. South of Thornton Avenue the blocks are large and almost empty (295, 296A, 296B, 335A, 335B, 336), bounded by Clawson, Woodbine and Randolph Roads and Stilford Avenue. The buildings are almost all detached frame dwellings with a few outbuildings, drawn mostly on large lots; a few larger houses stand on the diagonal Park Avenue. One firm is named, a carpet cleaning and mattress and feather renovating works (Benj. H. Mumford and Son) on the west side of Arlington Avenue near Rose Street. A fire alarm box stands at Arlington Place and several dashed lines mark 6-inch water pipes in the streets. Blocks across the top and left edges are marked with the numbers of the neighbouring sheets (57, 58, 59 and 65). A compass rose with the north arrow is at upper left, and the scale bar and a Princeton Map Division stamp are at the bottom right.
notes: Printed scale is 100 feet to one inch; the fit gives about 3.96 px/ft, consistent with that.
Stilford Avenue is Stillford Avenue in current OpenStreetMap data.
Woodbine Avenue was left out of the control streets: its modern line is not at the drawn position near Park and Arlington Avenues.

Map, 100 ft. Park Av diagonal blocks, Evergreen, Martine, Clawson, Woodbine (left out, displaced). One part.

sheet-61.description: Sheet 61 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north lies toward the upper left (the compass rose is at the top). It covers the part of Plainfield around the junction of West 7th Street, West 8th Street and Plainfield Avenue, from Division and Liberty Streets in the north to Spooner Avenue at the bottom. The western two thirds is a regular grid of blocks numbered 329, 345 and 349 between West 7th and West 8th Streets, cut by Liberty, Plainfield Avenue and Irving Place. Plainfield Avenue curves southeast across the middle of the sheet and meets Randolph Road and Sheridan Avenue at the lower right. Field Avenue and Randolph Road run diagonally in the upper right, with Stelle Avenue between them; Stelle, Sheridan and Sherman Avenues run south through large, mostly empty tracts (344, 342A, 342B, 388) that are shown divided into narrow lots without buildings. The built-up blocks are detached frame dwellings, many with small outbuildings marked auto houses, and a few larger houses with brick or stone parts. Fire alarm boxes are shown at Liberty Street and at Spooner Avenue. Water pipes (6 and 12 inch) are drawn dashed in the streets. Neighbouring sheet numbers 30, 36, 38, 56 and 62 are printed at the edges, and the scale bar is at the lower right with a Map Division stamp.
notes: Printed scale is 100 feet to one inch; the fit gives about 3.96 px/ft.
The north arrow points to the upper left; the fitted rotation is about -39 degrees.

Map, 100 ft. W 7th, W 8th, Division to Spooner; Field Av and NE Stelle Av left out. One part.

sheet-62.description: Sheet 62 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It shows the southwestern edge of the built-up city of Plainfield where it meets Piscataway Township in Middlesex County. Grant Avenue runs down the middle of the upper two thirds of the sheet and crosses West 7th Street, West 8th Street, Stelle Avenue, Sheridan Avenue and Sherman Avenue at right angles; Spooner Avenue forms the right margin and Hobart Avenue the left. The blocks are numbered 371, 372, 372A, 350 and 343, with the two long, narrow blocks 342A and 342B between Stelle Avenue and Sheridan Avenue, divided into lots but with almost no buildings. In the upper left blocks there is a row of dwellings along the north side of West 7th Street, and a handful of houses stand in the blocks near Spooner Avenue. South of Sherman Avenue the plan changes: Grant Avenue turns southwest, with Maltby Avenue parallel to it and Pemberton Avenue running off to the southeast, and the large blocks 374 to 377 are empty. The Plainfield and Piscataway Township boundary is lettered across the lower left corner. A fire alarm box stands at Grant and Sherman Avenues. The north arrow and compass rose are at the lower right, with the scale bar and a Map Division stamp; neighbouring sheet numbers 40, 43, 44, 61 and 64 are printed at the edges.
notes: Printed scale is 100 feet to one inch; the fit gives about 3.98 px/ft.
Hobart Avenue is not in the modern OpenStreetMap data and was not used as control.

sheet-63.description: Sheet 63 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It covers a district of Plainfield between Monroe Avenue at the top and Clinton Avenue at the bottom, with South 2nd Street on the far left and West 6th Street at the right edge. South 2nd, West 3rd, West 4th, West 5th and West 6th Streets run down the sheet, crossed by short east-west streets (Manson Place, Morris, Mc Dowell, Halsey, Bergen, Stanley Place and Lexington Place). The west half has dense small lots and blocks numbered 447 to 452 with mostly detached frame dwellings; Clinton Place at the bottom has a row of small houses on narrow lots. The Monroe Avenue M.E. Church, with a heating note (steam, gas and electric lights), stands on the south side of Monroe Avenue. East of West 4th Street the blocks 362, 363, 364, 366, 367 and 368 are large and almost empty, with only a few buildings along West 5th Street and in the lower right. Fire alarm boxes appear at Monroe Avenue and at the lower left corner near Evona Street. Dashed lines show 6 inch water pipes. A compass rose with the north arrow is at the top, the scale bar at the bottom, and a Map Division stamp at lower right. Neighbouring sheet numbers 41, 43, 45, 47 and 64 are printed at the edges.
notes: Printed scale is 100 feet to one inch; the fit gives about 3.97 px/ft.
Mc Dowell is McDowell Street, Morris is Morris Street, Bergen is Bergen Street and Halsey is Halsey Street in the modern OpenStreetMap data.
Morris and Mc Dowell Streets meet West 3rd Street as an offset crossing about 12 m apart.
The sheet is turned; the fitted rotation is about -44 degrees.
Map, 100 ft. Monroe to Clinton, S 2nd to W 6th. One part.

sheet-64.description: Sheet 64 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It shows the southern edge of Plainfield between Monroe Avenue near the top and Clinton Avenue at the bottom, with West 6th, West 7th and West 8th Streets running down the sheet and Sherman Avenue slanting across the right side. A diagonal dash-dot line lettered City of Plainfield and Piscataway Township, Middlesex County crosses the lower half from the southwest to the northeast and marks the boundary of the city. The blocks 369 and 370 between West 6th and West 8th Streets are long and narrow, with dwellings along the streets and the rest of the lots empty. Block 371A at the top, between Hobart Avenue and Monroe Avenue, has a small group of dwellings, and block 373 between West 8th Street and Sherman Avenue is mostly open ground with a few outbuildings, a hen-house group and a few dwellings near its south end. Beyond Sherman Avenue in the lower right a few scattered houses and farm buildings stand along Tompkins Avenue. The compass rose and north arrow are at the upper left. Dashed lines show 6 inch water pipes along West 7th and West 8th Streets. Neighbouring sheet numbers 43, 62, 63 and 61 are printed at the edges.

sheet-65-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 65 is the larger lower part of the sheet, below the heavy line that crosses it from the left edge to the right edge. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top, tilted slightly to the left. It shows Plainfield south of the railroad, between Randolph Road along the line and South End Avenue at the bottom. The west side has regular blocks 399B and 399C between Cameron Avenue, Lenox Avenue and Park Avenue, with detached dwellings on long narrow lots; Laramie Road crosses them and a row of dwellings stands along its south side. Park Avenue runs the full height of the sheet, with the long narrow blocks of tract 399A to its west. East of Park Avenue the most prominent feature is Muhlenberg Hospital (tract 297A): a main building with operating room, wards, kitchen, laundry, nurses home and isolation and tuberculosis buildings, with a heating and fire protection note (steam, gas and electric lights, city water, fire buckets, hose). Moffett Avenue crosses the east side, below which blocks 297B and 297C are mostly empty, with Marion and Florence Avenues and Leonard Place. A narrow strip between the heavy line and Randolph Road shows the ends of Stilford and Hillside Avenues. The compass rose and north arrow are at lower left; neighbouring sheets 60, 51 and 53 are named along the top.
notes: Printed scale is 100 feet to one inch; the fit gives about 3.98 px/ft.

sheet-65-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 65 is the strip above the heavy line that crosses the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing to the upper left. It shows a neighbourhood north of the railroad whose streets are not continuous with those below the line: Sumner Avenue, Emerson Avenue and Leland Avenue run roughly east-west with the heavy railroad line along the bottom edge, and Midway, George, Columbia Avenue and North Avenue cross them toward the northeast. The blocks 161A, 161B, 161C, 165, 167 and 169 are mostly narrow lots with detached dwellings, those on Emerson Avenue standing in a close row with house numbers in the 240 to 300 range. The Netherwood Reformed Church, with a note on heating and lighting, stands on the west end of Emerson Avenue. A fire alarm box is drawn at the foot of George and the railroad crossing at Leland Avenue. Beyond the railroad line the neighbouring sheet numbers 51 and 53 are printed; block numbers 159A, 159B and 43 are printed at the left and top edges. Earle Place is a short street at the lower left. Water pipes are shown dashed.

sheet-66-1.description: Sheet 66, part 1, the top half of the sheet, shows the industrial strip along the Central Railroad of New Jersey at the western edge of Plainfield, between West Front Street at the top and South 2nd Street at the bottom, west of Rock Avenue, which runs down the right edge. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper right. The many tracks of the railroad cross the middle of the part, with a siding curving off towards the works. North of the tracks stand The Lake Pigment Co. (store rooms, cooper shop, mixers and filters, shipping and mixing rooms, engine and coal house), the Plainfield Brass Foundry, a hay house and two dwellings. South of the tracks the long erecting, machine and boiler shop, pattern and stock rooms and offices of the Ransome Concrete Machinery Co., makers of contractors' machinery, fill the block. The boundary between the City of Plainfield and Piscataway Township, Middlesex County, crosses the part diagonally as a dash-dot line.
